## INTRODUCTION

The Commission hasissued aConsultativeDocument inviting comments on draft proposals for changing the capital adequacy rules currently applicable to securities dealers under Section 65Bof theSecurities Ordinance.TheConsultative Document also contains proposals for futures dealers and advisers.

This pamphlet provides a simplified outline of the proposals. Persons interested in more detail should examine the ConsultativeDocument.

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

## OBJECTIVES&amp;NEEDS

The proposed rules have been designed with certain objectives and needs in mind.

## Objectives

- To ensure dealersshould have sufficientcapital tocover their risks
- To provide relief from the existing requirements where itis due
- To reinforce good market practice
- To be forward looking and cover new activities and risks

## Needs

- To retain familiar ideas where possible
- Tobalance appropriate risk management(complexity) and simplicity

## WHATARETHEEXISTINGRULES?

- Securities dealers must maintain net capital and a liquidity margin in excess of $5M ($1M for sole proprietors) and $0.5M ($0.1M for sole proprietors) respectively.
- Net capital (NC) is the excess of approved assets (AA) over ranking liabilities (RL).

NC=AA-RL

- Liquidity margin (LM) is the excess of liquid assets (LA) over ranking liabilities (RL).

LM=LA-RL

- Approved assets, liquid assets and ranking liabilities are defined in detailin a Noticeissued by the Commission [The Securities (Specification of Approved Assets,Liquid Assets and Ranking Liabilities) Notice 1990].
- Discounting factors("haircuts")of between 20 and 100 per cent are applied to securities owned by the dealer ("house positions"). In addition, amounts due from third parties who settle forcash are reduced by 100 per cent after they have been outstanding for more than5 days (the well-known"5"day rule).

## WHYCHANGEEXISTINGRULES?

The existing rules have significant deffciencies from a risk management point of view.

## Examples are

- They treat major intermational dealers and small agency dealers alike
- They are too harsh in measuring the risks of holding "house positions"
- They are too harshin measuring the risk that a cashclient orotherbrokerwillnot payagainst deliveryof securities purchased
- They donot pick upsufficiently the risks associated with undertakinglarge volumes of business compared with smallvolumes
- Theydonotmeasure off-balancesheetrisks
- They do not give dealers credit for using hedging techniques toreduce risk

In addition, the two-tier test for capital and liquidity is duplicative,cumbersome and uses arbitrarymeasures

## THEPROPOSALS

- To replace the existing net capital and liquid margin testsbyasingleliquidcapital requirement
- Tolink the newliquid capitalrequirement withthelevel of business undertaken by the dealer (but only after a minimum level of activity is reached)
- Dealers to have liquid capital in excess of

$3M for corporations ($500,000 for sole proprietors);or whichever is the greater (see Illustration I)

5% of all liabilities (forcorporations and sole proprietors)

- To relax significantly the existing haircuts applied to a dealer's house positions (see Illustration I)
- Torelax significantly the existing discount applied to a dealer's accountsreceivable against delivery(seellustrationII)
- Tointroduce requirements foroff-balance sheet risks; and
- To give dealers credit for hedging techniques where appropriate

## COMPARISONOFCURRENTNETCAPITALANDPROPOSEDLIQUID CAPITAL (cont'd)

Notes on comparison

- (a)The proposed rules marks a relaxation of the existing harsh basis of calculating house securities positions.In this example where the dealer holds investments mainly in equities listed in Hong Kong, there is an increase in liquid assets resulting from the reduction in the haircut from 40% to 25%.
- (b)Receivables from brokers and cash clients which are included in liquid assets show a significant increase in the proposed rules.This is because of the more relaxed ageingreduction scalefor such receivables.
- (c)It is proposed to accept receiyables from margin clients up to the discounted value of the underlying collateral.This will provide a reasonable cushion for the position cum counterparty risks exposed by the dealer.
- (d)In the proposed rules,counterparty risksrelating to accounts payable havebeen recognised in the same way as for accounts receivable.
- (e)The proposed rules recognise off balance sheet exposures which are not properly recognised in the current rules.

## TESTINGTHEPROPOSALS

Theproposals were tested usingthelatest balance sheets of securities dealers.On this basis it was found that:

- Over97%of soleproprietors wouldcomplywith theproposed requirements and would not have toinjectadditional capital at their existing level of business (299 out of 308 in number).
- 8 of the 9 who would not have complied with the proposed requirements were having difficulty in complyingwith the currentrequirements.
- requirement.Of these,80 per cent would comply with the 15per cent of securities dealerswould trigger the5per cent proposed requirements.
